nodes.label: Web Console
nodes.rationale: The broad operational workbench for runs, changes, verification, hosts, policies, cost, devices, and immutable audit; requires a registered user-verified WebAuthn assertion for action confirmation and is Axe-checked to WCAG 2.0/2.1 A/AA plus 2.2 AA on every core route.

nodes.label: Native SwiftUI iOS App
nodes.rationale: The focused safety client for attention, proof-first run inspection, device security, notifications, and signed action review; signs with its paired device key and requires device-owner authentication for server-designated high-risk actions.

nodes.label: Capability-Gated Navigation (repair.ready)
nodes.rationale: Neither client invents capability: navigation and controls come from authenticated server state, Repairs stays completely absent until the server reports a fresh available repair.ready capability, and unknown, stale, unavailable, or revoked inputs fail closed.

nodes.label: Signed Action Review Contract
nodes.rationale: Review shows the exact target, effect, risk, parameter hash, expected state, and expiry; HTTP acceptance is only queued work, execution renders only with a daemon-derived receipt, and expiry, changed content, host loss, revocation, or acknowledgement ambiguity never triggers an automatic re-sign or resubmit.

nodes.label: Draft-Only Repair Publication
nodes.rationale: Publication is a high-risk signed action bound to the repair's exact state version and hash; it can only create a draft pull request — LoopGuard cannot merge or deploy it — and an ambiguous response is reconciled by action ID rather than publishing again.

nodes.label: Deprecated cloud-app Compatibility Fallback
nodes.rationale: cloud-app remains available for one release as an explicit fallback with no silent redirect; no new production architecture, security, or workflow behavior may be added to it, and it is removed only in a later, separately announced release.
